concepts.def: Visual Arts internal assessment; HL submits 8-11 resolved artworks; SL 4-7; coherent presentation in physical or virtual space.
Up to 700-word written statement explaining intent, themes, choices of presentation and connections among works.
Brian O'Doherty's Inside the White Cube 1976 critiques the neutral gallery; standard since MoMA's 1930s Alfred Barr installations.
Salon densely stacks works floor-to-ceiling (Paris Salon 1737); minimalist isolates each piece at eye-line for sustained contemplation.
Documenta Kassel founded 1955 by Arnold Bode; Venice Biennale since 1895; established global curatorial benchmarks.
Robert Smithson's 1968 Site/Non-site; works responsive to architectural and social context (e.g. Olafur Eliasson Weather Project Tate 2003).

walkthroughs.body_html:
Exhibition — a core area of Art & Design.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Exhibition brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Exhibition.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the significance of Duchamp's 'Fountain'?
options: It demonstrated his sculpting ability.
It is a study of plumbing.
The space between letters.
It challenged the definition of art - the artist's choice, not their skill, becomes the artwork.
A whole typeface that looks formal.
The space between letters.
It is a study of plumbing.
The small projecting line at the end of letter strokes.
